incident: Referee blows final whistle six minutes early
description: Brazilian referee Gilberto de Almeida Rego blew for full time around the 84th minute with France's Marcel Langiller clean through on goal; after furious French protests the players were recalled and the remaining minutes were played out. Argentina won 1-0.

incident: Antonio Rattin sent off
description: German referee Rudolf Kreitlein dismissed Argentina captain Rattin for 'violence of the tongue' despite speaking no Spanish; Rattin refused to leave for around 10 minutes and sat on the Queen's red carpet. Fed Argentine claims of European bias ('el robo del siglo') and directly led to the invention of yellow and red cards.
video_source: FIFA official YouTube (World Cup Rematch full match)

incident: Van de Kerkhof cast protest and Gonella's match control
description: Argentina delayed kick-off by protesting Rene van de Kerkhof's arm cast (worn without objection in five earlier games); referee Sergio Gonella upheld the complaint and made him add extra bandaging. Gonella's performance was widely criticised as weak and home-leaning; the Netherlands skipped the post-match ceremony. Gonella later denied conspiracy claims, noting Rensenbrink hit the post at 1-1.

incident: Hand of God goal
description: Diego Maradona punched the ball over Peter Shilton for Argentina's opener; Tunisian referee Ali Bin Nasser and linesman Bogdan Dochev both missed the handball and the goal stood. Maradona credited 'the hand of God'. Argentina won 2-1 and went on to win the tournament.

incident: Maradona goal-line handball not punished
description: Maradona blocked a goal-bound Soviet header on his own line with his hand ('Hand of God II'); Swedish referee Erik Fredriksson missed it - no penalty and no red card. Maradona later admitted it. Argentina won 2-0.

incident: Codesal penalty for Sensini's challenge on Voller
description: Mexican referee Edgardo Codesal awarded West Germany a late penalty for Roberto Sensini's sliding challenge on Rudi Voller - widely seen as soft or a dive; Brehme converted the only goal. Codesal had earlier waved away a similar Argentine appeal (Calderon), and his appointment (his father-in-law sat on FIFA's referees' commission) fuelled Argentine conspiracy claims.

incident: Monzon and Dezotti red cards
description: Pedro Monzon (65') became the first player ever sent off in a World Cup final for a challenge on Klinsmann, who was accused by Argentines of exaggerating; Gustavo Dezotti (87') received a harsh second red for wrestling the ball from Kohler at a throw-in. Argentina finished the final with nine men.

incident: Beckham red card after Simeone provocation
description: After Diego Simeone's heavy challenge, David Beckham flicked a leg at him and was sent off by Kim Milton Nielsen while Simeone received only a yellow; Simeone later admitted play-acting ('the referee fell into the trap'). Ten-man England held 2-2 and Argentina advanced on penalties.

incident: Sol Campbell goal disallowed
description: Campbell headed England in front late on but referee Kim Milton Nielsen ruled it out for Alan Shearer's elbow/foul on goalkeeper Carlos Roa - a call still disputed in England (Campbell has even suggested corruption). Match finished 2-2 and Argentina won the shootout.

incident: Ortega penalty appeal, dive booking and red card
description: Ariel Ortega went down over Jaap Stam's challenge in the box and was booked for diving as Argentina appealed for a penalty; when Edwin van der Sar rushed over to confront him, Ortega headbutted the keeper and was sent off. Bergkamp's 90th-minute winner followed almost immediately. The dive/penalty judgment is still argued; the red card itself was clear-cut.

incident: Penalty against Pochettino for challenge on Owen
description: Pierluigi Collina awarded England a penalty when Michael Owen went down over Mauricio Pochettino's challenge in Sapporo; Beckham converted for a 1-0 England win. Pochettino insists he never touched Owen and that VAR would have overturned it; Owen later signed a photo of the incident 'You definitely touched me'.

incident: Tevez offside goal allowed
description: Carlos Tevez headed in from a clearly offside position; referee Roberto Rosetti and assistant Stefano Ayroldi let the goal stand even after the stadium big screens replayed the offside, sparking Mexican protests on the pitch. Argentina won 3-1. The incident intensified calls for video technology.

incident: Neuer's aerial challenge on Higuain - no penalty
description: Manuel Neuer raced out and punched the ball clear while kneeing Gonzalo Higuain in the head inside the box; Italian referee Nicola Rizzoli gave the foul against Higuain rather than a penalty or card for Argentina. Germany won 1-0 in extra time.

incident: Rojo handball - no penalty after VAR check
description: The ball struck Marcos Rojo's hand off his own header in the Argentine box; referee Cuneyt Cakir consulted the VAR monitor and gave no penalty. Nigeria protested wildly and John Obi Mikel called it a clear penalty. Rojo then scored the 86th-minute winner that sent Argentina through and Nigeria out.

incident: Three first-half goals disallowed for offside
description: Lautaro Martinez (twice) and Messi had first-half goals ruled out by semi-automated offside technology, including one where Lautaro's shoulder was judged fractionally off; fans and some pundits argued the nearest defender kept him onside. The calls were technically correct per SAOT but the millimetre margins were fiercely debated. Saudi Arabia won 2-1.

incident: VAR penalty for Szczesny's contact on Messi
description: Referee Danny Makkelie awarded Argentina a penalty after a VAR review of Wojciech Szczesny's follow-through brushing Messi's face as both went for a high ball - widely panned as precisely what VAR was not brought in for; Szczesny (who bet Messi it would not be given) saved the spot-kick. Argentina won 2-0.

incident: Mateu Lahoz loses control - record 18 yellow cards
description: Spanish referee Antonio Mateu Lahoz issued a World Cup-record 18 yellow cards plus a red in the 'Battle of Lusail'; both teams raged at him, Messi said FIFA should not let him referee again, and Lahoz was reportedly sent home from the tournament. He also overlooked a possible Messi handball, and his generous stoppage time preceded the Netherlands' 90+11 equaliser. Argentina won on penalties.

incident: Soft penalty for Dembele's challenge on Di Maria
description: Referee Szymon Marciniak pointed to the spot when Angel Di Maria went down under minimal contact from Ousmane Dembele; Messi converted the opener. French media and pundits called it soft, though analysts noted it was not the kind of call VAR overturns.

incident: Encroachment claim against Messi's extra-time goal
description: French outlets and fans argued Messi's 3-2 goal should have been disallowed because Argentine substitutes stepped onto the pitch before the ball crossed the line; IFAB clarified the law only applies if they interfere with play. Marciniak later produced a photo showing seven French players on the pitch during an Mbappe goal. A French petition for a replay went nowhere.

incident: VAR-checked early penalty to Argentina
description: Argentina were awarded an 8th-minute penalty for Stefan Posch's foul on Lautaro Martinez, confirmed after a VAR check; Messi fired wide. Austrian players and fans felt the contact was minimal.

incident: Messi's record goal stands despite foul claim in build-up
description: Messi's record-breaking 17th World Cup goal (passing Klose) was allowed to stand despite Peter Schmeichel and others arguing Alexis Mac Allister had brought down Schlager in the build-up; FIFA-aligned analysis countered that Mac Allister won the ball first. Argentina won 2-0.

incident: VAR-awarded penalty for foul on Senesi
description: After a VAR review, Jordan's Nizar Al Rashdan was penalised for a foul on Marcos Senesi in the box; Lautaro Martinez converted to make it 2-0. Jordan contested the intervention. Argentina won 3-1.

incident: Egypt goal disallowed by VAR for foul at the other end of the pitch
description: With Egypt 1-0 up, Mostafa Zico's breakaway goal was ruled out after VAR found Marwan Attia had tugged Lisandro Martinez's shirt and stood on his foot roughly 20 seconds earlier, about 100 yards from goal. Match commentators said the intervention was beyond VAR's normal remit; Sky Sports judged it 'rightly disallowed'. Referee Francois Letexier. Argentina came from 2-0 down to win 3-2.

incident: No review of foul claim on Salah before Argentina's winner
description: Egypt appealed for Enzo Fernandez's 90+2 winner to be pulled back for a Lisandro Martinez foul on Mohamed Salah seconds earlier - a near-mirror of the earlier VAR intervention that had gone Argentina's way - but no review came. The Egyptian FA said it 'cannot remain silent' and filed an official complaint against referee Letexier's team.

incident: Embolo 'mistaken identity' red card for simulation
description: Referee Joao Pinheiro booked Paredes for a foul on Breel Embolo, but VAR showed Embolo falling before contact; using the mistaken-identity mechanism the caution was transferred and Embolo - already booked - was sent off for simulation, the first such dismissal at a World Cup. Swiss coach Murat Yakin said the decision 'destroyed the game'. Argentina beat the 10 men 3-1 in extra time.

incident: Officiating scrutiny around Elfath appointment
description: American referee Ismail Elfath took charge amid scrutiny of his unbeaten record in Messi matches (5-0 before kick-off); England fans accused him of letting Argentina 'get away with murder', while post-match analyses found no major errors and the VAR made no on-field interventions. Part of wider - and unproven - claims that officiating favoured Argentina throughout the tournament. Argentina won 2-1.
